column2: How do I locate at once the places that have no position on the map?
column3: Map → “📍 Places to locate” (or the dashboard → “Municipalities to complete” → 📍 Locate…, or Lists → Places): the places without a position, grouped by likely municipality thanks to the municipality reference shipped with the app. “✓ Locate here” for one place, “☑ Review and locate in a batch…” for several (only the “sure” ones are ticked); “↶ Undo” puts everything back. Nothing is located without your click, and nothing is searched online unless you allow it in ⚙️ Settings, place by place.

column2: How do I see the family’s occupations on a map, century by century?
column3: Charts → New → Maps → “🔨 Occupations on the map” → “From the app” tab → “Take this data”: a pie chart per municipality, one colour per main sector (the classification of the Occupation tree); the ▶ slider goes through the centuries one by one. A click on a municipality gives its occupations. Settings: by occupation family, a single occupation and its variants, a small map per century, where to place the occupation. From an old occupation’s sheet: “🗺 Where it was practised”. Never a living person or a confidential sheet.

column2: How do I see my father’s line and my mother’s line on a map, and where they meet?
column3: Charts → New → Maps → “👫 The two lines side by side” → “From the app” → “Take this data” (or, on a person’s sheet: ⋯ → “👫 Their two lines on the map”): father’s side in blue, mother’s side in orange; the municipalities where both lines passed are circled, and the ▶ slider shows them getting closer decade after decade. Also: the four grandparents, two people, two names, two lists. Settings: overlaid, side by side or ⇆ swipe; same municipality, same time or within a few km. A living starting person is never a dot.
